thread.title: Federal Reserve Will Prove Whether Stock Prices Are Silly Cheap or Value Traps

author: thestreet.com
title: Federal Reserve Will Prove Whether Stock Prices Are Silly Cheap or Value Traps
text:
Jerome Powell: the destroyer of "cheap" stocks or liberator of untapped value.
One of these will be true as the market digests the new Federal Reserve chairman 's comments to the media after the FOMC's decision on interest rates Wednesday. If the early February market correction was any indication, investors are willing to quickly switch to a bearish posture on fears of a hawkish Fed. Then again, investors have sent stocks higher from the February lows on prospects for strong U.S. growth.
Powell will probably be the ultimate decider on near-term market sentiment. It's hard to deny that at least on paper, stock prices are too cheap to ignore provided Powell doesn't sound too hawkish.
The S&P 500 forward price-to-earnings ratio continued to contract in February, and at just under 17 times, is at its lowest levels since late 2016 points out Bank of America Merrill Lynch. That puts the forward price-to-earnings ratio 11% above its long-term average.
Adds BofA strategist Savita Subramanian,"Despite the S&P 500 remaining expensive vs. its own history, stock selection opportunities for value investors today are at post-crisis highs. Valuation dispersion (based on forward EPS yield) for S&P 500 stocks has been climbing for the past three-and-a-half years, and now sits at its highest levels since 2009. This suggests a wide array of opportunities to differentiate between cheap and expensive stocks."
So get on out there and buy up those "cheap" dividend stocks such as IBM ( IBM ) and Action Alerts Plus holding Apple ( AAPL ) . That is until Powell tells you to do otherwise.
Source: BofA
